$notes: Human-authored, versioned rules table. A model never decides what to recommend, only how to word it. Every rule ships with static copy so the product works with no LLM.

Triggers: {metric, op, value} compares the raw metric value; {metric, category} compares the engine-derived z-category ('low' z<-1, 'typical', 'high' z>1) or an appearance category ('low'/'moderate'/'high', or a Norwood stage bucket). All triggers in a rule must fire (AND). min_confidence defaults to the metric's confidence_floor.

safety_tier: 1 self-directed, 2 OTC with irritation profile, 3 clinician territory (named, never dosed), 4 surgical/procedural (named, no links). Tier 3/4 never enter the ranked plan; they render in the 'To discuss with a professional' section.
cadence: 'daily' tasks define day completion; 'weekly' tasks have a target count per week; 'once' tasks are one-off setup. opens_week staggers tasks so week 1 is never overwhelming.
excludes: rule ids suppressed when this rule fires. always_on: fires regardless of findings when goal matches (foundational habits).
Copy must pass copy/voice.md: no comparative language, no 'mog', no 'subhuman', no degrading tiers, no dosing, no caloric figures.

rules.task_title: Hit your protein and movement targets for the day

copy.headline: Lower body fat gradually
copy.body: The line between jaw and neck is mostly soft tissue. Losing body fat slowly, about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, with protein and resistance training, sharpens it more than anything done to the jaw.
copy.why_this: Your facial adiposity reads high and your jaw-neck angle is wide. Both move as body fat drops.

rules.task_title: Hit your protein and movement targets for the day

copy.headline: Lean out gradually
copy.body: Facial fat is among the most changeable things about a face. Lose slowly, about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, with protein and lifting to keep muscle.
copy.why_this: Your facial adiposity reads above the typical range.

rules.task_title: Resistance training session

copy.headline: Lift three times a week
copy.body: Three full-body sessions a week keep fat loss showing as definition, not a drawn look.
copy.why_this: Keeping muscle is what makes fat loss look sharp.

copy.headline: Jaw exercisers
copy.body: Placeholder entry so the exclusion graph has a target. Tier X: never emitted.

rules.task_title: Broad-spectrum SPF 30+ on face and neck

copy.headline: Daily broad-spectrum SPF
copy.body: Sun is the main driver of uneven skin over time. Broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every morning, cloudy days included.
copy.why_this: Foundational for every skin goal.

rules.task_title: Gentle cleanse and moisturise, morning and night

copy.headline: A two-step routine, twice a day
copy.body: A gentle, fragrance-free cleanser and a plain moisturiser, morning and night. Most unevenness is irritation and dryness, and the basics clear much of it in a few weeks.
copy.why_this: Your skin evenness reads below typical. Basics first; actives once the barrier settles.

rules.task_title: Evening active (start 2–3 nights a week)

copy.headline: Add one over-the-counter active, slowly
copy.body: One evening active: adapalene gel for texture and breakouts, or low-strength azelaic acid for redness and tone. Start two or three nights a week and build up. Some dryness or flaking early on is normal. Stop and see a pharmacist or dermatologist if irritation is more than mild.
copy.why_this: Your skin evenness reads low. These have the best evidence of anything sold without a prescription.

rules.task_title: In bed by your target time

copy.headline: Protect your sleep
copy.body: Sleep-deprived faces are rated less healthy in controlled studies, mostly around the eyes. A consistent bedtime does more than any product.
copy.why_this: Fast and free. Shows in the eye area first.

rules.task_title: Hydrate; go easy on sodium and alcohol in the evening

copy.headline: Reduce morning puffiness
copy.body: Evening salt, alcohol and short sleep show under the eyes next morning. Water through the day, less salt late, a regular bedtime. Eye creams are mostly moisturiser.
copy.why_this: The low-effort part of the eye area. Sleep is the high-return part.

rules.task_title: Tidy brows: remove strays between and below, keep the shape

copy.headline: Tidy the brows, don't reshape them
copy.body: Remove strays between the brows and below the arch; leave the shape alone. Thinned brows read older and more tired.
copy.why_this: Immediate and reversible. It frames the whole eye area.

rules.task_title: Book a haircut

copy.headline: Get a cut that works with your proportions
copy.body: A good barber shifts how your proportions read. Long forehead: volume at the sides, not height. Short forehead: a little height on top. If the hairline is receding, don't cover it; covering reads as hiding.
copy.why_this: Reversible and fast.

rules.task_title: Hair: no heat today, condition if you wash, style without pulling

copy.headline: Treat the hair you have gently
copy.body: None of this regrows hair. It makes the hair you have look fuller: a gentle shampoo, conditioner, little heat, and no tight styles that pull at the hairline.
copy.why_this: You asked about hair. Zero risk, and it shows within weeks.

copy.headline: Hairline recession: treatments exist, and they work best early
copy.body: Your hairline reads at a stage where recession is visible. Two treatments have strong evidence: topical minoxidil, sold over the counter, and oral finasteride, prescription-only, with side effects worth a real conversation. A dermatologist or GP can advise in one appointment; earlier is better. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Hairline stage estimated at Norwood 3 or above.

rules.task_title: Take a hairline reference photo in the same light

copy.headline: Keep an eye on the hairline
copy.body: A mature hairline is normal, not recession. Time tells the difference: the same reference photo, a few weeks apart. If it moves, have the treatment conversation early.
copy.why_this: Hairline estimated at Norwood 2, within normal adult variation.

rules.task_title: Retake your best photo from further back with 2× zoom

copy.headline: Shoot from further back
copy.body: At arm's length a phone makes the nose read about thirty percent wider and shrinks the ears and jaw. Step back a metre or more and zoom in, or have someone else shoot.
copy.why_this: Measured in a 2018 JAMA study.

rules.task_title: Find your window: soft light from slightly above and to one side

copy.headline: Use soft, slightly directional light
copy.body: Flat frontal light erases structure; hard overhead light exaggerates it. Use window light from slightly above and to one side, and face it.
copy.why_this: After distance, light matters most in how structure photographs.

rules.task_title: Posture check: ears over shoulders, chin level

copy.headline: Bring your head back over your shoulders
copy.body: Forward head posture softens the jaw-neck line. Ears over shoulders, chin level, not lifted. Nothing structural changes; how it is seen does, at once.
copy.why_this: Free and immediate. If your jaw-neck angle reads wide, some of that is posture.

rules.task_title: Shape the beard: keep length along the jaw, fade the cheeks and neck

copy.headline: Let the beard do the jaw's work
copy.body: Facial hair can widen and square the lower face. Keep density and a little length along the jaw and chin, fade the cheeks, and set the neckline a finger above the Adam's apple.
copy.why_this: Your jaw reads narrower than typical against the cheekbones. The beard can carry the line.

rules.task_title: Try growing stubble along the jaw for two weeks

copy.headline: Consider stubble along the jaw
copy.body: Stubble along the jaw and chin adds visual width where your face is narrowest. Two weeks shows whether it suits you.
copy.why_this: Jaw width reads narrow against the cheekbones, and you are clean-shaven.

copy.headline: About mewing
copy.body: Tongue-posture routines are promoted for a profile like yours. The British Orthodontic Society and the American Association of Orthodontists both said in 2025 there is no scientific evidence they change adult facial shape. Good head posture is worth having; expecting bone to move is not.
copy.why_this: Your profile convexity reads outside the typical range, the finding these routines are marketed to.

copy.headline: Profile convexity: an orthodontist can tell you what it is
copy.body: Your profile reads markedly convex. That can be jaw position, teeth or soft tissue, and only a clinical assessment can tell which. An orthodontic consultation is often free or inexpensive. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Soft-tissue facial convexity measured well below the typical range.

copy.headline: Chin projection
copy.body: Your chin sits well behind the nose-to-chin reference line. A board-certified facial plastic or maxillofacial surgeon could assess it. Posture and facial hair change how it reads without changing anything. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Soft-tissue chin measured more than 6 mm behind the E-line.

copy.headline: Nose-lip angle: a camera note
copy.body: Your nose-lip angle reads more acute than typical. That is structure. How it photographs can change: keep the camera at or slightly above eye level.
copy.why_this: Nasolabial angle below the typical range.

copy.headline: Nose width and camera distance
copy.body: Your nose base reads wide against your eye spacing. Close-up phones distort this most, about thirty percent at arm's length, so photos from further back will differ from selfies. This was measured at a controlled distance.
copy.why_this: Nasal base width above the typical range.

rules.task_title: Find your better side in soft, even light

copy.headline: Everyone is asymmetric; light decides how much it shows
copy.body: Every face is asymmetric, and uneven light exaggerates it. Even frontal light minimises it. Most people have a side that photographs better; find yours.
copy.why_this: Symmetry reads a little below typical. The lighting check passed, so this is not a capture artefact.

rules.task_title: Lip balm with SPF

copy.headline: Don't forget the lips
copy.body: Chapped lips read as unhealthy and are the easiest thing here to change. A plain balm with SPF, when you apply sunscreen.
copy.why_this: A small addition to the skin routine.

rules.task_title: Water with every meal

copy.headline: Drink water with meals
copy.body: The evidence that hydration changes skin is weaker than the internet says. Mild dehydration does show in the face by evening, and ruling it out costs nothing.
copy.why_this: Supporting habit. It costs nothing.

rules.task_title: No alcohol tonight

copy.headline: Cut back on alcohol
copy.body: Alcohol adds calories, disrupts sleep and causes next-day puffiness. Fewer drinking days is the version people keep.
copy.why_this: Facial adiposity reads high. Alcohol is a common hidden contributor.

copy.headline: Prescription retinoids: worth asking about
copy.body: Your skin evenness reads well below typical. The best-evidenced treatment for texture and tone is prescription tretinoin, and persistent breakouts have prescription options too. A dermatologist or GP, often by telehealth, can prescribe. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Skin evenness index below 0.50.

rules.task_title: Reference photo: same spot, same light, same distance

copy.headline: One reference photo a week
copy.body: Not a scan. A plain photo in the same spot, light and distance each week. It stays on your phone and is never analysed.
copy.why_this: Keeps the eight weeks honest without daily re-scanning.
